subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm deciding to keep the vehicle model static without a joint skeleton, since it's a boxy armored truck design that doesn't need rigging complexity—just a solid, safe structure around 5.2 units.

Now I'm laying out the truck's dimensions and part breakdown: 6 wheels at 0.55 radius, a lower hull box, and an upper cabin built from an extruded side profile to get that blocky, angular silhouette with a sloped windshield and hood.

Defining the hull extrusion profile...

I'm adding a rear water tank made from a horizontal cylinder mounted at the back, plus a roof-mounted cannon turret with a glowing cyan barrel tip, and a tinted windshield plane angled to match the cabin's slope.

Normalizing the normal vector confirms the direction and up vectors for the slope plane. Now I'm planning the side details: dark window slits, a decal texture for "RIOT CTRL" text and a corporate emblem on the doors, plus neon accents—alternating red/blue roof bar, cyan/magenta side strips, magenta underglow, and yellow-white headlight slits, along with a dark wedge bumper plow.

For the wheels, I'm positioning dark cylinders with glowing magenta hub rings and dark fender arches, placing three axles along the body length so the body sits just above the wheel centers. I'm also adding roof rack cage details, an antenna, riot-mesh window shields with grid texture, and rear elements like a hose reel, red taillights, a ladder, and small side water nozzles.

I want to add armor plates and a spotlight mounted on the cannon, and I'm planning several textures—hazard stripes, a logo emblem, "RIOT CONTROL" text, and the window mesh grille. For the paint scheme I'm going with a cyberpunk palette: dark gunmetal/navy body panels with yellow, cyan, and magenta accents, using a panelled countershade material for the body and a yellow lower stripe.

Writing paint logic and body extrusion...

Still positioning wheels and fenders...

Now I'm adding the cannon turret on the roof, with a rotating base cylinder and a barrel rod extending forward with a thicker nozzle housing.

Clears the barrel over the windshield fine, then adds support yoke cheeks on the turret sides. Positions a front roof light bar with alternating red/blue glow segments, nudging it to z .5 to avoid overlapping the turret base. Now considering a front bumper plow wedge shape.

Building the hazard-textured bumper box, grille with glowing cyan slits, and headlight glow boxes positioned on the front face, with the hood surface sloping up from the headlight line.

Now I'm adding hood vents and side plates with "RIOT CONTROL" logos, working through the geometry math to make sure the text orientation reads correctly when viewed from the side rather than mirrored.

Working out window placement relative to the body's sloped profile, sizing the glass planes with a dark teal glow, then adding an amber grid-line cage texture over the side window plane.

Now I'm adding rear details: red glow light bars, a license plate texture, rear bumper and a ladder structure, plus underglow magenta boxes beneath the body and cyan side strips near the skirt line.

I'm placing more neon accents -- magenta strips along the sides, cyan edges on the roof, vertical tail corner lights, roof light bars, and considering a holographic rooftop sign with fictional cyberpunk branding like "NEOCORP" for extra flavor.

Now I'm sketching out the texture plan: hazard stripe patterns, a corp logo emblem for the doors, and side text decals like "RIOT CONTROL," plus setting wheel geometry so they sit flush with the ground. Aiming to keep the code around 350 lines total before writing it out.

I'm defining a box helper function to quickly spawn parts with position and color, confirming static models can skip joints entirely since nothing needs to articulate.

Still writing the glow helper call...

Now I'm building the cannon rod, the alternating red/blue light bar segments, and the barrel rings positioned along a direction vector from the base to the muzzle.

The nozzle needs a tapered rod shape with a glowing cyan disc at the tip, and I'm considering whether to add water-spray elements but may skip the mist cone for simplicity. I'm placing the wheels at specific z-coordinates matching the front and rear axles, mirroring the light positions across the sides, then finalizing everything.
